slug: 2021-01-01 Building Resilient CRVS Systems amid COVID-19 - Namibia (Technical Brief)

facts.fact: The brief (Bayer Forsingdal and Munyika, for the Centre of Excellence for CRVS Systems, APAI-CRVS and ECA) states that four years after the 2010 launch of the digitisation project the online, integrated electronic NPRS was fully functional and installed in 95 per cent of civil registration offices; it gives no count of offices.

The brief reports 64,283 birth records entered in the electronic birth register of the NPRS in January to August 2020 (92,616 in the same months of 2019, 77,224 in 2018; all ages, with amendments and some duplicates) and, from NPRS operational statistics, 14,033 deaths registered in January to August 2020.

The brief describes registration at the civil registration office: the registrar validates the application, pulls the e-notification data into the online NPRS, captures the remaining data and at once issues an electronically printed certificate, in under five minutes; the process is undated and is dated here to the brief's 2020 study period.

The brief states that the digitisation project that produced the electronic NPRS was launched in 2010 and led jointly by the Office of the Prime Minister and the Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security, and was completed in 2014.

The brief states that after the state of emergency of 17 March 2020 a total of 22 birth and death registration offices at health facilities were temporarily closed, only regional and sub-regional offices stayed open, and late registration and duplicate certificates were suspended; most services were restored by September 2020.

systems.owner: Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security
systems.tiers: regional and sub-regional civil registration offices and registration offices at health facilities; installed in 95 per cent of civil registration offices by 2014; civil registration and identity management are one system

systems.owner: health authorities notify; the NPRS receives
systems.tiers: 51 maternity wards at health centres and 19 clinics; introduced 2017; 178,929 births notified since

systems.owner: health authorities and police mortuaries notify; the NPRS receives
systems.tiers: health facilities and police mortuaries; piloted 2018; 22,823 deaths notified since; causes coded to ICD-11

systems.owner: Office of the Prime Minister and Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security
systems.tiers: 2010 to 2014; historical manual records digitised and all civil events placed under one profile linked to the ID production system

systems.system: Electronic data exchange between the NPRS and the Namibia Statistics Agency
systems.owner: Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security and Namibia Statistics Agency, under a memorandum of understanding
systems.tiers: national; the agency has drawn annual vital statistics reports from NPRS data since 2016
